title: US officials accuse Iran-linked actors of stepping up attacks on critical infrastructure
actor: Iran-linked actors (alleged by US DHS Secretary Mullin)
summary: In written testimony to the House Homeland Security Committee, reported by Bloomberg and Etnews, DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said Iranian government-linked cyber actors and pro-Tehran criminals have targeted US infrastructure since February. Etnews adds the testimony says criminals increasingly use AI to scale attacks. Officials said no evidence ties recent outages to attacks.
plain: A US cabinet official told Congress that Iran-linked hackers have been going after US hospitals, water, energy, transport and banks more since February.
exec: Official warning of heightened Iran-linked targeting of critical sectors; raises the threat level for operators in them.
action: Operators of water, energy, healthcare, transport and finance systems: keep internet-exposed control systems off the internet and follow the current FBI and CISA Iran advisories.
impact: Statement of rising targeting; no specific victims or technical details given in the reporting read.

validation.note: Asharq News reporting Mullin's written testimony as cited by Bloomberg; the testimony itself was not read. Etnews (19 Nov) independently reports the same testimony, adds the AI point and Iran-linked focus since February; the testimony itself was not read. Both relay one testimony, so still single_source.

review.note: Compared Mullin attribution, written testimony, since-February, sectors, 18 Nov date, AI point (Etnews) and officials' no-evidence-of-attack line (Asharq/Reuters) against Asharq and Etnews
